Bromine is a chemical element; it has symbol Br and atomic number 35.

Gabapentin: Pfizer. Gabapentin is a
central nervous system (CNS) depressant and derivative of the inhibitory neurotransmitter, GABA.
In which country is IAI Kfir?
Who is credited with discovering Penicillin?
Penicillin: Alexander Fleming. Penicillin was discovered in 1928 by the Scottish physician Alexander Fleming as a crude extract of P. rubens.
2C-B: Alexander Shulgin. 2C-B, also known as 4-bromo-2,5-dimethoxyphenethylamine or by names such as Nexus or Erox, is a psychedelic drug of the phenethylamine and 2C families.
Who is credited with discovering Chromium?
Chromium: Louis Nicolas Vauquelin. Chromium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cr and atomic number 24.

Despite resembling an unrelated shrub in leaf and flower shape, this shade-loving carrot-family plant has spread worldwide as an invasive garden escapee since being introduced as an ornamental — what is it?
Aegopodium podagraria is a species of flowering plant in the carrot family Apiaceae that grows in shady places.
These mostly semiaquatic vertebrates are tetrapods that pointedly lack an amniotic membrane, splitting into just three living orders like the frogs and toads of Anura — what are they?
Amphibian are ectothermic, anamniotic, four-limbed vertebrate animals that constitute the class Amphibia.

Once classified as bacteria and originally called archaebacteria, this domain of mostly single-celled prokaryotic organisms turns out to be the ancestral lineage from which eukaryotes evolved — which domain of life?
Archaea (ar-KEE-) is a domain of organisms.
Born in 1655, this Italian instrument maker earned lasting fame for inventing a keyboard instrument that could play both soft and loud — who was he?
Bartolomeo Cristofori (Italian; May 4, 1655 - January 27, 1731) was an Italian maker of musical instruments famous for inventing the piano.
Caused by a recessive allele in the leopard but a dominant one in the jaguar, this dark melanistic variant still secretly carries its usual rosettes — what is it called?
Black panther is the melanistic colour variant of the leopard (Panthera pardus) and the jaguar (Panthera onca).
Every one of this genus's seven woody species is toxic enough to rival deadly nightshade, and none survive in the wild anymore — only in gardens — which genus?
Brugmansia is a genus of seven species of flowering plants in the nightshade family Solanaceae.

This group of diseases directly affecting the heart muscle itself may show few symptoms early on but can progress to heart failure, irregular heartbeat, and an increased risk of sudden cardiac death — what condition is it?
Cardiomyopathy is a group of primary diseases of the heart muscle. In dilated cardiomyopathy the ventricles enlarge and weaken.

Once prized as refrigerants and aerosol propellants — Freon being the famous example — these halogenated compounds were phased out under the Montreal Protocol for gnawing holes in the ozone layer — what are they?
Chlorofluorocarbon (CFCs) and hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs) are fully or partly halogenated hydrocarbons that contain carbon (C), hydrogen (H), chlorine (Cl), and fluorine (F).

This icy small body from the outer Solar System develops a glowing atmosphere called a coma, and sometimes a tail, as it warms and releases gases when passing near the Sun — name this celestial object?
Comet is an icy, small Solar System body or interstellar object that warms and begins to release gases when passing close to the Sun, a process called outgassing.
A bright yellow polyphenol found in turmeric, a member of the ginger family, this compound is sold as an herbal supplement, cosmetic ingredient, food flavoring, and food coloring — which compound?
Curcumin is a bright yellow chemical produced by the plant species Curcuma longa.
Known from thousands of fossils pulled from the La Brea Tar Pits, this extinct species of canine roamed the Americas until about 10,000 years ago. Name the species?
Dire wolf (Aenocyon dirus) is an extinct species of canine which was native to the Americas during the Late Pleistocene and Early Holocene epochs (125,000-10,000 years ago).
Working with George de Hevesy, this Hungarian chemist theorized that diffusion speed depends on a nuclide's mass and became the world's go-to expert at preparing polonium — who was she?
Elizabeth Rona (20 March 1890 - 27 July 1981) was a Hungarian nuclear chemist, known for her work with radioactive isotopes.
Distinct from secretion, this bodily process includes exhaling carbon dioxide, sweating, and passing urine through the bladder and urethra — what's it called?
Excretion is elimination of metabolic waste, which is an essential process in all organisms.
This American political scientist argued in a controversial 1992 book that the spread of liberal democracy and free markets might be the final form of human government — who is he?
Francis Fukuyama (born October 27, 1952) is an American political scientist, political economist, and international relations scholar.

This metabolic pathway builds glucose from non-carbohydrate sources, occurring mainly in the liver in vertebrates, and serves as one of the body's two main tools for maintaining blood sugar — what process is it?
Gluconeogenesis (GNG) is a metabolic pathway that results in the biosynthesis of glucose from certain non-carbohydrate carbon substrates.

Also called the harlequin or multicoloured Asian type, this exceptionally variable insect established itself across Africa and South America after being introduced beyond its native Asia — what species?
Harmonia axyridis is a lady beetle or ladybird species that is most commonly known as the harlequin, Asian, or multicoloured Asian lady beetle.

This broad academic category studies human society, culture, and its fundamental questions — during the Renaissance, the term specifically meant the study of classical literature and language as a secular alternative to religious studies. Name the category?
Humanities are academic disciplines that study aspects of human society and culture, including certain fundamental questions asked by humans.

This pathogen has caused seasonal flu in humans and also infects birds and some mammals; strains circulate constantly in bats, pigs, horses, and dogs. It was the cause of the Spanish Flu pandemic from 1918 to 1920. What is it?
Influenza A virus is a pathogen with strains that cause seasonal flu in humans; it can also infect birds and some mammals.
Best known for his laws of planetary motion, this German astronomer has also been called the 'father of science fiction' for his novel Somnium. Who is he?
Johannes Kepler (27 December 1571 - 15 November 1630) was a German polymath who was an astronomer, mathematician, astrologer, natural philosopher and music theorist.
Named after the American endocrinologist who identified it in the 1940s, this chromosome anomaly, also called 47,XXY, typically affects phenotypic males with infertility. What condition is it?
Klinefelter syndrome (KS), also known as 47,XXY, is a chromosome anomaly.
At the time of her death, this French heiress and cosmetics-empire shareholder was the richest woman in the world, worth over $44 billion. Who is she?
Liliane Bettencourt (ne Schueller; 21 October 1922 - 21 September 2017) was a French heiress, socialite and businesswoman.
Which group of vividly colored, long-tailed New World parrots — prized in aviculture though some species face conservation concerns — belongs to the tribe Arini?
Macaw are a group of large New World parrots that are long-tailed and often colorful, in the tribe Arini.
Ranging from Patagonia to Bolivia during the Ice Age, this genus of giant ground sloths includes a type species that could weigh nearly four tonnes — which genus?

Megatherium (meg--; from Greek mga 'great' + theron 'beast') is an extinct genus of large ground sloths endemic to South America that lived from the Early Pliocene through the end of the Late Pleistocene.
This New World songbird mimics the calls of other species, insects, and frogs, and serves as the state bird of five U.S. states — which bird?
Mockingbird are a group of New World passerine bird from the family Mimidae.

It's the inherent character of the universe as a whole — the laws, elements, and phenomena of the physical world, including life itself — even though humans are often spoken of as somehow apart from it. What is it?
Nature is an inherent character or constitution, particularly of the ecosphere or the universe as a whole.
Despite counting the killer whale and pilot whale among its roughly forty species, this marine mammal family is more closely related to porpoises than to true whales — what family is it?
Oceanic dolphin are a widely distributed family of dolphins that live in the sea.
Located above, below, between, and behind the eyes, these four paired air-filled cavities take their names from the skull bones that contain them — what are they?
Paranasal sinuses are a group of four paired air-filled spaces that surround the nasal cavity.

This insect order's scientific name derives from the Ancient Greek word for 'apparition' or 'phantom' — fitting for a group whose members are famous for disguising themselves as twigs and leaves. What order is this?
Phasmatodea (also known as Phasmida or Phasmatoptera) are an order of insects whose members are variously known as stick insects, stick bugs, walkingsticks, stick animals, or bug sticks.

This large, nearly ubiquitous family of flowering plants provides the world's cereal crops, bamboo, and the plants used in lawns and pastures, ranking as the fifth-largest plant family with roughly 12,000 species — what family is this?
Poaceae (poh-(y)e), also called Gramineae (gr-(y)e), is a large and nearly ubiquitous family of monocotyledonous flowering plants commonly known as true grasses.
This Gram-negative, rod-shaped bacterium selectively blocks antibiotics from crossing its outer membrane, making it a notorious cause of hospital-acquired pneumonia — what is it?
Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a common encapsulated, Gram-negative, aerobic-facultatively anaerobic, rod-shaped bacterium that can cause disease in plants and animals, including humans.

Almost exclusively affecting girls and emerging between 6 and 18 months of age, this genetic disorder, caused mainly by mutations in the MECP2 gene, brings repetitive movements, slowed growth, and language impairment — which condition?
Rett syndrome (RTT) is a genetic disorder that typically becomes apparent after 6-18 months of age and almost exclusively in girls.
Named for the Latin word for willow tree, from which it was first derived, this plant hormone is both a precursor to aspirin and a common ingredient in anti-acne skincare — which compound?
Salicylic acid is an organic compound with the formula C7H6O3.
Setting a world record for mental calculation at London's Imperial College in 1980, this self-taught Indian prodigy also wrote books on math, puzzles, and astrology — who is she?
Shakuntala Devi (4 November 1929 - 21 April 2013) was an Indian mental calculator, astrologer, and writer, popularly known as the "Human Computer".
This family of roughly 1,450 moth species, with narrow wings and streamlined bodies built for fast, hovering flight, are so nimble they're routinely mistaken for hummingbirds — what are they called?
Sphingidae are a family of moths commonly called sphinx moths, also colloquially known as hawk moths, with many of their caterpillars known as hornworms.
These large waterfowl of the genus Cygnus are close relatives of geese and ducks, and are known for typically mating for life. What birds are they?
Swan are birds of the genus Cygnus within the family Anatidae.
Writing in 1798, this English cleric-economist warned that abundance only fuels population growth, eventually restoring poverty and hardship for the lower classes — who is he?
Thomas Robert Malthus (13/14 February 1766 - 29 December 1834) was an English economist, cleric, and scholar influential in the fields of political economy and demography.

Entering Soviet service in the 1960s, this jet was the USSR's first supersonic bomber to reach production, though it disappointed with poor range and proved notoriously hard to fly — what aircraft is it?
Tupolev Tu-22 (Air Standardization Coordinating Committee name: Blinder) was the first supersonic bomber to enter production in the Soviet Union.
Leading organic chemistry at DuPont's Experimental Station, this troubled chemist not only invented nylon but also helped lay the groundwork for neoprene. Who was he?
Wallace Carothers (April 27, 1896 - April 29, 1937) was an American chemist, inventor, and the leader of organic chemistry at DuPont, who was credited with the invention of nylon.

First identified in 1789 and not manufactured at scale until the 1920s, this corrosion-resistant, silvery-grey metal resembles hafnium and takes its name from the mineral that remains its main source — what element, symbol Zr, is it?
Zirconium is a chemical element; it has symbol Zr and atomic number 40.
Made by the adrenal glands, this hormone powers the fight-or-flight response — boosting blood flow to muscles, dilating pupils and raising blood sugar by hitting alpha and beta receptors. What is it?
Adrenaline: Hormone and medication. It appears as a white microcrystalline granule.
This Austrian psychotherapist broke from Freud's circle to found 'individual psychology,' emphasizing birth order and coining the term 'inferiority complex' — who was he?
First identified as a chemical in 1887 and later marketed as the drug Benzedrine, this CNS stimulant is prescribed today for ADHD and narcolepsy — which drug?
Designed in 1957 by a Soviet bureau and known to NATO as 'Coke,' this 50-seat twin-turboprop airliner is still license-built in China under a different name — which aircraft?
Antonov An-24: Soviet turboprop airplane. The aircraft was manufactured by the Kyiv, Irkutsk and Ulan-Ude Aviation Factories.
Also nicknamed the toddy cat or musang, this small viverrid native to South and Southeast Asia is IUCN-listed as least concern yet still poached for the illegal wildlife trade — what is it?
Asian palm civet: Species of mammal.

Native to West and Central Africa, this nonvenomous constrictor is the smallest of its kind on the continent and earns its common name from its habit of curling into a tight coil when frightened — which species?
Ball python: Species of constricting snake.

With arms and tentacles up to 26 feet long held at right angles to its body, this deep-sea cephalopod has been spotted as deep as 6,212 meters — the only one of its kind known to survive the hadal zone. What is it?
Named for a Native American people of Oregon and Washington, this tandem-rotor heavy-lift helicopter grew out of Vertol's 1957 Model 107 design — what aircraft is it?
Boeing CH-47 Chinook: American tandem-rotor helicopter introduced in 1962 during the Cold War.
This group of roughly 20,000 non-vascular land plant species — liverworts, hornworts, and mosses — reproduces by spores instead of flowers or seeds. What is it called?
Bryophyte: Terrestrial plants that lack vascular tissue.
Once used in Italy for hunting large game and herding cattle, this mastiff breed today mostly serves as a guard dog or companion — which breed?
Cane Corso: Italian breed of mastiff. It is usually kept as a companion dog or guard dog; it may also be used to protect livestock.
Marked by patients who may lie motionless for days or repeat purposeless movements, this neuropsychiatric syndrome often responds to benzodiazepines or electroconvulsive therapy — which condition?
Native to the mountains of Honduras and Guatemala and nicknamed the 'custard apple' for its creamy texture, this fruit was called 'the most delicious fruit known to men' by Mark Twain — which fruit?
Cherimoya: Edible fruit-bearing species of plant.
This English inventor made the world's first slimline pocket calculator in 1972, then launched the UK's first mass-market home computer for under £100 — who is he?
Clive Sinclair: English entrepreneur and inventor (1940–2021)
A heavy-set, fox-like canid native to East Asia, this animal is named for its raccoon-like face markings and is unusual among canids for hibernating in winter and climbing trees. What is this animal?
Common raccoon dog: Canid indigenous to East Asia. Named for its raccoon-like face markings, it is most closely related to foxes.
Stalked ones anchored to the seafloor are nicknamed 'sea lilies' while the free-swimming kind are 'feather stars' — what's the class name for these mouth-on-top echinoderms?
This Canadian-born entrepreneur co-founded and serves as CEO of Roblox Corporation, after his earlier company was acquired by MSC Software in 1998 — who is he?

Cultivated in China for more than 2,000 years despite not being formally described until 1780, this tree produces the most widely grown fruit in its genus, known by names like Japanese or Chinese persimmon. Which species?
Diospyros kaki: Oriental fruit. Although its first botanical description was not published until 1780, D. kaki cultivation in China dates back more than 2000 years.
Belonging to the phylum Annelida and often called a 'nightcrawler' by anglers, this segmented soil-dweller is the classic bait fished from underground burrows — which invertebrate?

This discipline systematically applies science and math to design solutions like bridges, pacemakers, and spacecraft, with traditional branches in civil, mechanical, electrical, and chemical work — which field?
This small finch native to Europe and Asia is the original species to bear its common English name, and goes by 'plum bird' in Shropshire — what is it?
Eurasian bullfinch: Species of bird. The Eurasian bullfinch or common bullfinch (Pyrrhula pyrrhula) is a small passerine bird in the finch family, Fringillidae.
Native to North African deserts from Western Sahara to the Sinai, this diminutive canid uses its oversized ears to shed heat and detect prey burrowing underground — which species is it?
Fennec fox: Species of fox. The fennec fox (Vulpes zerda) is a small fox native to the deserts of North Africa, ranging from Western Sahara and Mauritania to the Sinai Peninsula.

Madagascar's largest carnivore is a slender, long-tailed mammal that climbs down trees head-first and has convergently evolved so many cat-like features it's been likened to a small cougar — yet it's no cat. What is it?
Fossa (animal): Cat-like, carnivorous mammal endemic to Madagascar.

This digestive disorder involves weak stomach muscle contractions that delay how quickly food empties into the intestine, often linked to nerve damage from uncontrolled diabetes — what's the condition called?
Gastroparesis: Medical condition. The opposite of this, where stomach contents exit quickly into the duodenum, is called dumping syndrome.
The simplest and only non-chiral of the 20 proteinogenic amino acids, this compound makes up about 35% of collagen's amino acid content — what is it?
Glycine: Amino acid. In the body, glycine plays several crucial roles.
Breeders prefer to call it a 'cavy,' and despite its name it hails from the Andes rather than West Africa and isn't related to swine at all — which Andean rodent is it?
Guinea pig: Domesticated rodent from South America.
Comprising cicadas, aphids, bed bugs, and more than 80,000 other species with piercing-sucking mouthparts, which insect order is nicknamed the 'true bugs'?
Hemiptera: Order of insects often called true bugs.
Often called the founder of alpinism and modern meteorology, this Genevan scientist is also credited with building the first successful solar oven — who was he?
Horace Bénédict de Saussure: Genevan scientist and mountaineer (1740–1799)
Marked in its severe stage by hallucinations and paradoxical undressing, which condition is defined as a body core temperature below 35 degrees Celsius?
Hypothermia: Human body core temperature below 35 °C (95 °F)
Symbol Fe, atomic number 26, it's the most common element on Earth by mass and forms much of the planet's core — yet smelting it needs furnaces 500°C hotter than copper does. Which metal?
Iron: Chemical element with atomic number 26 (Fe)
Despite its name, this is actually a species of sunflower native to central North America, grown across temperate zones for its edible tuber — also called a sunchoke. What is it?
Jerusalem artichoke: Species of sunflower native to eastern North America. It is cultivated widely across the temperate zone for its tuber, which is used as a root vegetable.
The first woman of Indian origin to fly to space, she served as a mission specialist on two Space Shuttle Columbia flights, the second ending in the 2003 disaster that killed her — who was she?
About 1.5 metres long and beginning at the cecum via the ileocecal valve, this final section of the human gut absorbs water and salt before waste reaches the rectum — what part of the body is it?
Large intestine: Last part of the digestive system in vertebrates.
The only person ever to win two unshared Nobel Prizes, this American chemist earned one for his work on the chemical bond and another for peace activism — who is he?
Linus Pauling: American scientist and activist (1901–1994)
Described in the New Testament as a physician, this traditional author of two New Testament books is said to have been martyred by hanging from an olive tree — who is he?
Luke the Evangelist: One of the four traditionally ascribed authors of the canonical gospels.

Often called the mirror image of depression, this psychiatric state brings racing thoughts, pressured speech, boundless energy, and a shrinking need for sleep — what is this elevated mood syndrome called?
Mania: State of abnormally elevated or irritable mood, arousal, and/or energy levels.
Developing from pigment-producing skin cells and most common on the legs in women and the back in men, about 30% of cases of this cancer arise from existing moles — what is it?
Melanoma: Skin cancer originating in melanocytes.
Succeeding the Castro brothers, this engineer became Cuba's first head of state in nearly six decades who wasn't a member of that family — who is he?
Miguel Díaz-Canel: Leader of Cuba since 2021.
Named for its rough alignment with the Moon's cycle — the two words are even linguistic cognates — this calendar unit varies from 28 to 31 days in the Gregorian system — what is it?
Month: Unit of time, usually 28 to 31 days.
Made of the same tough protein as claws, hooves, and horns, this protective plate covers the tip of your fingers and toes — what is it?
Nail (anatomy): Hard keratin protection of digit.
Surrounded by a typically darker-colored areola, this raised region of breast tissue is where milk exits through the lactiferous ducts during lactation — what is it?
Nipple: Part of the breast. The milk can flow through the nipple passively, or it can be ejected by smooth muscle contractions that occur along with the ductal system.
Sold under the brand name Prilosec, this proton-pump inhibitor treats acid reflux and peptic ulcers — what is it?
Omeprazole: Medication to treat gastroesophageal reflux disease and other conditions.
Located behind the stomach, this gland is 99 percent exocrine yet still secretes insulin and glucagon to regulate blood sugar — which organ?
Pancreas: Organ of the digestive system and endocrine system of vertebrates.
Harvested from Penicillium moulds and brewed in deep tanks, this β-lactam was among the first medicines to knock out staph and strep infections. What is it?
Penicillin: Group of antibiotics derived from fungi.
Known across South Asia as Indian gooseberry or amla, this deciduous tree is native to tropical regions of the continent — which plant?
Phyllanthus emblica: Berry and plant. Phyllanthus emblica, commonly known as emblic, Indian gooseberry, amalaki, amloki, or amla, is a deciduous tree of the family Phyllanthaceae.
This birth defect results in one or more extra fingers or toes and has been linked to at least 39 different genetic mutations — what is it called?
Polydactyly: Physical anomaly involving extra fingers or toes.

Native to western Eurasia and a member of the rose family, this species — the wild or sweet cherry — is the ancestor of the sour cherry, though every part of the plant except its ripe fruit is mildly toxic. What is it called?
Prunus avium: Species of flowering plant in the rose family. The species is often cultivated as an ornamental tree.
Also known as hexogen, this nitroamine explosive is the key energetic agent in C-4 and a core ingredient of Semtex — which compound?
RDX: Explosive chemical compound. RDX (Research Department Explosive or Royal Demolition Explosive), or hexogen, also known by other names, is an organic compound with the formula (CH2N2O2)3.
This branch of medicine handles more than 100 inflammatory diseases of the bones, muscles, and joints — like lupus and arthritis — and overlaps heavily with immunology. What is it?
Rheumatology: Medical speciality of inflammatory diseases.
Known as 'swede' in British English, this root vegetable is a hybrid of cabbage and turnip — what is it?
Rutabaga: Root vegetable in the Brassica family.
This group of autoimmune diseases causes thickened skin and poor blood flow to the fingers and toes, with one form known as CREST syndrome — what is it called?
Scleroderma: Group of autoimmune diseases resulting in abnormal growth of connective tissue.
Despite historians noting that email already existed in the early 1970s, this MIT-trained engineer holds a 1982 copyright and claims to have invented it as a teenager — who is he?
Shiva Ayyadurai: American engineer, conspiracy theorist, and entrepreneur.
Raised in the Bronx by Puerto Rican-born parents after her father's early death, this Princeton and Yale Law graduate became the third woman ever named to the U.S. Supreme Court — who is she?
Sonia Sotomayor: US Supreme Court justice since 2009.

Often triggered by medications like lamotrigine or allopurinol, this severe skin reaction starts with flu-like symptoms before the skin begins to blister, peel, and affect mucous membranes — what is this condition called?
Stevens–Johnson syndrome: Skin disease. The most common cause is certain medications such as lamotrigine, carbamazepine, allopurinol, sulfonamide antibiotics and nevirapine.
Rolled out in March 2023 and designed to replace Turkey's F-16 fleet, this fifth-generation stealth fighter made its maiden flight in February 2024 — what is it?
TAI TF Kaan: Turkish fighter aircraft.
This group of inherited blood disorders reduces hemoglobin production and is classified as alpha or beta depending on which globin gene is deficient. What condition is it?
Thalassemia: Family of inherited blood disorders. Symptoms depend on the type of thalassemia and can vary from none to severe, including death.

A nightshade cousin of tobacco and chili peppers, its edible berry was carried from western South America to Eurasia by the Spanish during the Columbian exchange — which fruit, eaten as a vegetable, is it?
Tomato: Edible berry. The tomato (US:, UK:; Solanum lycopersicum) is a plant whose fruit is an edible berry that is eaten as a vegetable.
A member of the ginger family native to the Indian subcontinent, its boiled and dried rhizomes are ground into a deep orange-yellow powder used to color and flavor curries — what is it?
Also called vervain, this genus of roughly 150 flowering plant species is native mostly to the Americas and Asia, though its European type species grows wild there too — what genus is it?
Verbena: Genus of plants. Verbena, also known as vervain or (in obsolete spelling) verveine, is a genus in the family Verbenaceae.

With black-tipped wings and long red legs and bill, this long-distance migrant famously avoids the open Mediterranean, detouring instead via Gibraltar or the Levant on its way to African wintering grounds — which bird is it?
White stork: Species of bird. The white stork (Ciconia ciconia) is a large bird in the stork family, Ciconiidae.
Marketed under the brand name Imovane, this 'Z-drug' sedative treats insomnia by boosting GABA activity in the brain much like a benzodiazepine, though it's chemically distinct — what is it?
The symbol for phosphorus is P. Phosphorus is a chemical element; it has symbol P and atomic number 15.
